paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Knowing God isn't just a feeling or a pile of facts, because the writer says, "By this we can be sure that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments." (1 John 2:3). Saying "I know Him" is easy, like me claiming I'm a world-class sprinter when my base is gold and does NOT move fast. Walking it out is what shows it, and whoever claims to abide in Him "must walk as Jesus walked." (1 John 2:6).

That walk has a clear shape: love. The writer says, "Whoever loves his brother remains in the light," and whoever hates his brother is in the darkness (1 John 2:10-11). I spent years in a junk drawer, friend, so I know darkness is no place to find your way around. The good news is that "the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining." (1 John 2:8), and the writer says sins "have been forgiven through His name." (1 John 2:12), so we walk in love because we've been forgiven, not to earn it.

Then comes the warning: "Do not love the world or anything in the world." (1 John 2:15). The world's pull is real, but "The world is passing away, along with its desires; but whoever does the will of God remains forever." (1 John 2:17). So here's your question for today, baker: what are you giving your love to? Hold the passing things loosely, keep walking in love, and stay close to the One who lasts.
